content: 1. Ostergaard L. conducted a study comparing two different methods for testing partners of individuals diagnosed with Chlamydia trachomatis. This research aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of these partner testing approaches in managing the infection. (Sex Transm Infect.) 2. Schwebke JR and Desmond RA performed a randomized controlled trial to assess various partner notification methods for the prevention of Trichomoniasis in women. The study provided insights into the effectiveness of these strategies. (Sex Transm Dis.) 3. Potterat JJ and Rothenberg R reported on the preliminary effectiveness of a self-referral system for identifying cases of gonorrhea. Their findings highlighted the potential utility of this approach in case detection. (Am J Public Health.) 4. Brown LB, Miller WC, Kamanga G, Nyirenda N, Mmodzi PP, Pettifor A, and colleagues demonstrated that HIV partner notification is both effective and feasible in sub-Saharan Africa. Their study emphasized the opportunities this approach provides for HIV treatment and prevention. (J AIDS.) 5. Landis SE, Schoenbach VJ, Weber DJ, Mittal M, Krishan B, Lewis K, and colleagues conducted a randomized trial in North Carolina to evaluate the outcomes of partner notification in cases of HIV infection. Their results provided valuable data on the effectiveness of this intervention. (N Engl J Med.) 6. Rosenberg NE, Mtande TK, Saidi F, Stanley C, Jere E, Paile L, and colleagues carried out an unblinded randomized controlled trial in Malawi to recruit male partners for couple HIV testing and counseling as part of the Option B+ program. The study explored strategies to enhance partner engagement. (Lancet HIV.) 7. Cherutich P, Golden MR, Wamuti B, Richardson BA, Ásbjörnsdóttir KH, Otieno FA, and colleagues conducted a cluster randomized controlled trial in Kenya to evaluate assisted partner services for HIV. Their findings highlighted the impact of this approach on partner notification and testing. (Lancet HIV.) 8. Schillinger JA, Kissinger P, Calvet H, Whittington WL, Ransom RL, Sternberg MR, and colleagues investigated the use of patient-delivered partner treatment with azithromycin to prevent recurrent Chlamydia trachomatis infections among women. This randomized controlled trial demonstrated the potential benefits of this intervention. (Sex Transm Dis.) 9. Golden MR, Kerani RP, Stenger M, Hughes JP, Aubin M, Malinski C, and colleagues conducted a community-level randomized trial in Washington State to assess the uptake and population-level impact of expedited partner therapy (EPT) on Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Their findings underscored the effectiveness of EPT in reducing infection rates. (PLoS Med.) 10. Clark JL, Segura ER, Oldenburg CE, Rios J, Montano SM, Perez-Brumer A, and colleagues performed a pilot randomized controlled trial in Lima, Peru, to evaluate the impact of expedited partner therapy (EPT) on partner notification among men who have sex with men (MSM). The study demonstrated an increase in partner notification frequency with EPT. (BMC Medicine.) 11. Golden MR, Whittington WLH, Handsfield HH, Hughes JP, Stamm WE, Hogben M, and colleagues examined the effect of expedited treatment of sexual partners on recurrent or persistent gonorrhea or chlamydial infections. Their findings highlighted the benefits of this approach in reducing reinfection rates. (N Engl J Med.) 12. Nuwaha F, Kambugu F, Nsubuga PS, Hojer B, Faxelid E conducted a study in Uganda to evaluate the efficacy of patient-delivered partner medication in treating sexual partners. Their research demonstrated the potential of this strategy in managing sexually transmitted infections. (Sex Transm Dis.)
